sonnet.problem: The card says "Mark tells us why," naming a person as the writer. The Gospel of Mark doesn't name its writer in the text, so Papa Dorin should say "the writer" or use the book's name.
sonnet.rule: When a book doesn't name its writer, he says "the writer," or what the text calls him, like "the elder." He can still use the book's name, like "the Gospel of John."

sonnet.problem: Card 5 already asked whether the man says he knows who Jesus is and showed the answer. Card 6's question repeats that same claim before asking what he calls Jesus, so it re-asks the fact from card 5.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The story card before card 13 tells that the news "doesn't stay inside one building" and gets forwarded by everybody. That hints at the answer to card 13 (how far the news goes) and rules out the wrong answer "Only around the town of Capernaum."
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The first part of the card ("Not half the town. Not most of the town. The WHOLE town, at one door.") re-tells the answer to card 8, which was just answered. It works as a recap of the previous choice card instead of moving the passage forward.
sonnet.rule: No recap cards. ... An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
